abstract: Let $d(a)$ be the natural density of positive integers whose Collatz orbit visits $a$, and let $U$ be the map between consecutive odd iterates. Fix a positive odd target $t$ prime to three and $P>0$. For every sufficiently large $X$ and all $k\ge1$, $s\ge2$ with $2^s3^k\le(\log X)^P$, a positive fraction of the starts in $(X,2X]$ congruent to $-1$ modulo $2^{s+1}3^k$ have exact $v_3(x+1)=k$, visit $t$, and begin with $s$ odd steps of valuation one. On these starts, $xd(x)$ is comparable to $(3/2)^k$ and both $x[d(U^2(x))-d(x)]$ and $x[d(U^s(x))-d(x)]$ are comparable to one. A subfamily of size at least a constant times $X/(2^s3^k\sqrt{\log X})$ has disjoint predecessor sets and common first-arrival times at $t$ on the odd, shortcut, and ordinary maps. For each fixed $D>0$, the relative gain at the first odd doubling can thus be of order $(\log x)^{-D}$ while $xd(x)$ is of order $(\log x)^D$, already for $t=1$. For the selected starts, the ratio of $xd(x)$ to their own normalized Syracuse atom at ternary depth $\lfloor\log_3 x\rfloor$ is uniformly bounded, and Collatz convergence remains open. The proof combines fixed-total inverse-word sampling, a uniform passage estimate, and a bounded expected occupation count for a parity walk. The supplement gives a lower-density argument for a smaller parameter budget and exact finite checks.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: How little a Collatz predecessor set can gain at its first odd doubling
